questions.question: A crawler targets one billion pages in 30 days. What average fetch rate should its initial capacity estimate use?
options: About 386 pages per second
About 12 pages per second
About 11,600 pages per second
Exactly 800 pages per second
questions.explanation: One billion divided by 30 days is about 386 fetches each second. A higher value such as 800/s is a deliberate peak-planning allowance, not the average.

questions.question: Which condition must hold before a URL is fetched in this design?
options: It is normalized, not already seen, allowed by policy, and eligible under its host budget
It has the highest global priority regardless of host state
A worker has idle CPU
Its content hash is already known
questions.explanation: The frontier combines URL admission with host-level eligibility. Global priority cannot bypass robots policy or the host's next-allowed time.

questions.question: Why does the design partition frontier ownership by host or registrable-domain hash?
options: One owner can coordinate that host's crawl delay and leases
It makes all hosts receive identical priority
It eliminates the need for a robots cache
It lets every worker retry the same URL
questions.explanation: Stable ownership gives one scheduler authority over a host's policy state, next-allowed time, and assignment lease.

questions.question: What is the correct response when a host returns repeated timeouts or 429 responses?
options: Back off with jitter per host and open a circuit after repeated failures
Retry immediately from every worker
Remove the host delay until the fleet catches up
Drop all URLs from every other host
questions.explanation: Transient failures should lengthen the affected host's next-allowed time and remain isolated from unrelated hosts.

questions.question: What problem does an exact content hash solve that URL normalization cannot?
options: Identical document bodies served from different URLs
Whether a URL's host is currently eligible
Whether robots.txt permits a path
Whether a worker lease is valid
questions.explanation: Different URLs can serve the same bytes. URL-level and content-level duplicate checks protect different parts of the crawl.

questions.question: Which metric best reveals that a crawler is respecting politeness rather than only maximizing throughput?
options: Host-delay compliance alongside eligible frontier age
Total discovered URLs only
Number of worker processes only
Object-storage capacity only
questions.explanation: Host-delay compliance shows whether the scheduler honors its remote-host contract, while eligible frontier age shows the cost of those choices.
